title: Constantinople, 381
hookLine: the council completes the Creed on the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life
carry: the lord and giver of life

lines: NICAEA, ON THE SON: LINE AFTER LINE.
cards: Read the creed of Nicaea to the end and something is missing. It spends line after line on the Son: God of God, begotten, not made, of one substance with the Father.

Then it reaches the Holy Spirit and says only: and in the Holy Spirit. For a while that was enough. Then some teachers began to say the Spirit was less than God: a power God uses, a holy servant, but not Lord.
So the bishops gathered again, this time in the emperor's new capital on the water. Today, the council that finished the sentence: Constantinople.

teach.b: The Catechism says the faith about the Spirit was confessed at the second ecumenical council, at Constantinople, in 381, and that the creed said at Mass comes from these first two councils together.
So the Nicene Creed is really Nicaea, finished at Constantinople.
The old Book of Common Prayer gives the added opening like this: "And I believe in the Holy Ghost, The Lord and giver of life."

Then, as the Catechism summarizes the council's words: who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son is worshiped and glorified, who has spoken through the prophets. Take the two titles one at a time.

Lord: the same title the creed gives the Son. Not a force, not an energy, not an errand runner. Lord, and worshiped together with the Father and the Son, which the creed would never say of a creature.

teach.h: THE BREATH OF LIFE IN GENESIS.
teach.b: Giver of life: that reaches back to the first pages of Genesis, where God shapes the man from the earth and "breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul."

teach.h: THE LORD AND GIVER OF LIFE.
teach.b: The Church hears the Spirit in that breath, and Catholics say the one who gave life in the beginning gives life now: in baptism, in prayer, in a dry heart that starts to move again.
As the Church tells it, the bishops didn't invent a new teaching. They said out loud what the Church already did when it baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

teach.h: THE THIRD NAME, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT.
teach.b: In the Church's telling: three names, one God, and the third is not an afterthought.

how: Catholics say the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed at Sunday Mass and may begin prayer or work with Come, Holy Spirit; the Spirit is invoked at every baptism and confirmation.

games.q: you're at Constantinople. some say the Holy Spirit is a holy power God uses, not God. how do you finish the creed's line on the Spirit?
o: a holy power sent by God.
the Lord and giver of life, worshiped with the Father and the Son.
leave it at and in the Holy Spirit.
games.why: the council confessed the Spirit as the Lord and giver of life, who with the Father and the Son is worshiped and glorified.

practice: Breathe slowly, noticing that this breath came without your deciding and the next is already on its way: on the in-breath, the Lord; on the out-breath, and giver of life.
If you pray, use the short traditional prayer, Come, Holy Spirit, and then stay quiet; if you don't, let the breath itself be enough to notice.
